updates.title: Drops are refused on an inactive technician and one removed from this location
preconditions: You are signed in as an Owner or Admin user whose role has Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit, at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
Your browser window is at least 1024 px wide, so the display switcher (List, Tech View, Board View) shows at the right of the Work Orders toolbar.
Technician {Technician-B} (for example Ralph Edwards) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
Customer {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST C96970 Refused Drops") is used by this case only.
Approved work order {Work-order-1} (for example S10043-17631) for {Customer-A} is led by technician {Technician-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST Ina Inactive).
Approved work order {Work-order-2} (for example S10043-17632) for {Customer-A} is led by {Technician-B}.
Approved work order {Work-order-3} (for example S10043-17633) for {Customer-A} is led by technician {Technician-C} (for example ZZAUTOTEST Mona Moved).
After the work orders were given their leads, {Technician-A}'s staff account was deactivated.
You pinned {Technician-C} in Board View, and after that {Location-A} was removed from {Technician-C}'s Location field. {Technician-C} is still active.
On the Work Orders page nothing is ticked in Status, Asset on Site shows no choice (if its chip shows Yes or No, click the x on the chip), Assigned to me is off and Search is empty.
steps: Open Work Orders, click the All tab and click Board View in the display switcher.
Type the name of {Customer-A} in Search.
Read the column headers of {Technician-A} and {Technician-C}.
Drag {Work-order-2} from {Technician-B}'s column onto {Technician-A}'s column and let go.
Read where {Work-order-2} is.
Drag {Work-order-2} from {Technician-B}'s column onto {Technician-C}'s column and let go.
Read the message that appears and where {Work-order-2} is.
Click Tech View in the display switcher.
Read the group headers of {Technician-A} and {Technician-C}.
Drag {Work-order-2}'s row from {Technician-B}'s group onto {Technician-A}'s group and let go.
Drag {Work-order-2}'s row from {Technician-B}'s group onto {Technician-C}'s group (the group holding {Work-order-3}) and let go.
Read where {Work-order-2} is.
Click {Work-order-2} to open it and read its Lead Technician.
results: Step 3: {Technician-A}'s column is still shown with {Work-order-1} and is marked inactive.
Step 3: {Technician-C} is not among the pinned columns. {Technician-C}'s column appears further along as a normal column holding {Work-order-3}, and it has no inactive marker.
Step 5: the drop is not accepted. {Work-order-2} goes back to {Technician-B}'s column.
Step 7: the drop is refused with the message "This technician can't be assigned work orders." and {Work-order-2} stays in {Technician-B}'s column.
Step 9: in Tech View {Technician-A}'s group is still shown with {Work-order-1} and is marked inactive.
Steps 10 to 12: neither drop is accepted. {Work-order-2} stays in {Technician-B}'s group.
Step 13: the Lead Technician of {Work-order-2} is still {Technician-B}.
updates.source: Epic SV-10043; stories SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician), SV-10046 (Story 3, Board View) and SV-10045 (Story 2, Tech View); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 49 (14 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S4-N5 (widened in version 49) and S3-R20c (added in version 49), both from Chris Ward's answer 2 of 14 Oct 2026 to our question sheet; S3-N2, S3-N4, S3-R20b, S2-N2 and S2-N3; read 14 Oct 2026. Sasha Grosman's answer to engineering of 24 Sep 2026 treated a technician who is no longer at this location like an inactive one; PRD version 49 (14 Oct 2026) says that column shows no inactive marker, and we take the later PRD as prevailing. Source-verified 14 October 2026. This version of the case has not yet been checked against a build (the previous version was last checked against build v26.40.8-7a95011 on 10/8/2026).
quotes: S3-N2
Keep matching work visible in its deactivated technician’s column.
S3-N4
Show an inactive indicator on deactivated technician columns.
S3-R20b
A pinned technician who is not enrolled at this location gets no column here. If they still lead work orders at this location, they appear as a normal, unpinned column holding that work.
S3-R20c

The column of S3-R20b takes no drops. Dropping a work order on it is refused with "This technician can't be assigned work orders." and the work order stays where it was. The column shows no inactive marker, because the technician is not deactivated (S3-N4). Once it holds no work orders, the column is no longer shown.
S4-N5
Nothing can be dropped onto the column/group of an inactive technician (S2-N2, S3-N2) or of a technician who is not enrolled at this location (S3-R20c).
S2-N2
Keep matching work visible under its deactivated lead technician.
S2-N3
Indicate deactivated technicians as inactive in group headers.
doc_part1: Sign in as an Owner or Admin user. On a QA site click the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView". To check the permissions: your initials (top right) > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders: View and Create & Edit are on.

Pick one location for the whole case; it is shown in the top bar next to the bell (to change it: your initials > Change Location). This is {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919). Create everything below at {Location-A}.
Use a desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide (narrower windows show only the List, with no display switcher).

Your initials > Settings > Staff. Create a new staff member for this case only (do not reuse a shared one, because this case changes the record): click New Staff Member and enter First Name and Last Name (for example ZZAUTOTEST Ina Inactive), an Email, Role Technician, Departments Service, Location {Location-A}, turn Time Clock on, then Save & Close. This is {Technician-A}.

Your initials > Settings > Staff. Reuse a staff member only if they are active, have Time Clock on, {Location-A} in Location and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User. Otherwise click New Staff Member and enter First Name and Last Name (for example Ralph Edwards), an Email, Role Technician, Departments Service, Location {Location-A}, turn Time Clock on, then Save & Close. This is {Technician-B}.

Your initials > Settings > Staff. Create a new staff member for this case only (do not reuse a shared one, because this case changes the record): click New Staff Member and enter First Name and Last Name (for example ZZAUTOTEST Mona Moved), an Email, Role Technician, Departments Service, Location {Location-A} and one other location {Location-B} (for example Staging Light Duty), so her Location field is never empty, turn Time Clock on, then Save & Close. This is {Technician-C}.

Top menu Customers > New Customer > Name (for example "ZZAUTOTEST C96970 Refused Drops") > Save. This is {Customer-A}; use it for this case only. On the customer page click Contacts > New Contact > First Name and Last Name (for example ZZAUTOTEST Contact) > Save. Then Assets > New Asset > pick the contact, Year (for example 2022), Make (type "Freight" and pick Freightliner), Model (for example M2), Unit (for example TRK-118) > Save. Contact and Make are required.

Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick {Customer-A} and its asset > Save (if a Confirmation about the credit limit appears, click Create). The work order opens on its Lines tab with the New Line form. In What Are You Doing? type "grease" and pick the ready-made line "Service - Full grease service", turn Line Approved on and click Save & Close. The status reads Approved. Write down the number shown at the top left (for example S10043-17631). Repeat this twice more. Number them {Work-order-1}, {Work-order-2} and {Work-order-3} in the order you create them.

On the work order page pick the technician in the Lead Technician dropdown; it saves at once. Give {Work-order-1} the lead {Technician-A}, {Work-order-2} the lead {Technician-B} and {Work-order-3} the lead {Technician-C}.

Work Orders > All tab > Board View. If three technicians are already pinned, unpin one (click the filled pin in its column header), because only three pins are allowed. Click the pin icon in {Technician-C}'s column header. Her column moves right after Unassigned with a filled pin.
Deactivate {Technician-A}: your initials > Settings > Staff > {Technician-A}'s edit icon > click Deactivate Account and confirm.
Remove {Location-A} from {Technician-C}: your initials > Settings > Staff > {Technician-C}'s edit icon > remove {Location-A} from her Location field (keep {Location-B}) > Save. She stays active.

Check the setup worked: Work Orders > All tab > Search with the name of {Customer-A} shows {Work-order-1} led by {Technician-A}, {Work-order-2} led by {Technician-B} and {Work-order-3} led by {Technician-C}. Settings > Staff shows {Technician-A} deactivated and {Technician-C} active without {Location-A}. If anything differs, fix it before you start, then clear the search.
doc_part2: Goal: one deactivated technician {Technician-A} and one active technician {Technician-C} removed from {Location-A} (pinned before the removal), each still leading one work order at {Location-A}; then drops of {Work-order-2} onto both in Board View and in Tech View.
GET /api/staff lists staff; each row has both id and staff_id, and the Schedule's staffId and the working-hours calls use staff_id.

Create {Technician-A} and {Technician-C} new for this case (never deactivate or move a shared technician). Create {Customer-A}, its contact and asset, and {Work-order-1} to {Work-order-3} on screen as in Part 1. Record {Work-order-1 id} to {Work-order-3 id}.
Pin {Technician-C} on screen (Board View column header pin icon) before removing {Location-A}; pins are per user and at most three.
UNVERIFIED on the Work Orders QA site: whether the Location field can be left empty, which is why {Technician-C} is given {Location-B} as well.

Steps 4 to 7: Playwright drag-and-drop from {Work-order-2}'s card to each column. Read the message text after the second drop exactly and compare it character for character with "This technician can't be assigned work orders." Record where the card ends up after each drop.
Steps 3 and 9: record each header's text and whether it shows an inactive marker or a pin. UNVERIFIED: how the build shows the inactive marker (a label or a badge); record what you see.
Steps 10 to 13: the same drags in Tech View on the rows; then open {Work-order-2} and read its Lead Technician. Confirm with GET on the work order that the lead did not change.
Context: this case follows PRD version 49 (14 Oct 2026). Nothing about how the build behaves today is assumed; judge only what you see.
Evidence: a screenshot after each step that has an expected result, the build marker, and the real value of every brace name.
updates.change_summary: Rewritten in full to the 8 Oct layout (link, Preconditions with {placeholders}, setup moved to the doc). PRD v49: pins {Technician-C} before removing her from the location (S3-R20b), expects the refusal message "This technician can't be assigned work orders." and no inactive marker on her column (S3-R20c), the work order staying with {Technician-B} (S4-N5 widened); the inactive half kept (S3-N2/S3-N4, S2-N2/S2-N3); own new ZZAUTOTEST technicians so no shared staff record is deactivated; quotes re-copied from v49; Rule 56 divergence sentence on Sasha's 24 Sep answer.

preconditions: You are signed in as an Owner or Admin user whose role has Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit and Schedule access, at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
Your browser window is at least 1024 px wide, so the display switcher (List, Tech View, Board View) shows at the right of the Work Orders toolbar.
Technician {Technician-A} (for example Esther Howard) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on, the Service department, and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
Technician {Technician-B} (for example Ralph Edwards) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on, the Service department, and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
Customer {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST S4R28 Approved Lines") is used by this case only.

Work order {Work-order-1} (for example S10043-17641) for {Customer-A} is led by {Technician-A} and has an approved line {Line-1} (for example "Service - Full grease service") and a line that is not approved, {Line-2} (for example "Service - Adjust clutch"), saved with Line Approved off.

Work order {Work-order-2} (for example S10043-17642) for {Customer-A} is led by {Technician-A} and has an approved line {Line-3} (for example "Service - Full grease service") and a declined line {Line-4} (for example "Service - Adjust clutch").

Work order {Work-order-3} (for example S10043-17643) for {Customer-A} is led by {Technician-A} and has two approved lines, {Line-5} (for example "Service - Full grease service") and {Line-6} (for example "Service - Adjust clutch").
{Technician-A} has a shift tomorrow 8:00–10:00 on {Work-order-1} that covers {Line-1} and not {Line-2}.
{Technician-A} has a shift tomorrow 10:00–12:00 on {Work-order-2} that covers {Line-3} and not {Line-4}.
{Technician-A} has a shift tomorrow 13:00–15:00 on {Work-order-3} made with Choose lines, with both {Line-5} and {Line-6} ticked.
No other shift is booked on {Work-order-1}, {Work-order-2} or {Work-order-3}.
On the Work Orders page nothing is ticked in Status, Asset on Site shows no choice (if its chip shows Yes or No, click the x on the chip), Assigned to me is off and Search is empty.
steps: Open Work Orders, click the All tab and click Board View in the display switcher.
Type the name of {Customer-A} in Search.
Drag {Work-order-1} from {Technician-A}'s column into {Technician-B}'s column.
Read the title of the question that opens.
Click Keep shifts.
Drag {Work-order-2} from {Technician-A}'s column into {Technician-B}'s column.
Read the title of the question that opens.
Click Keep shifts.
Drag {Work-order-3} from {Technician-A}'s column into {Technician-B}'s column.
Read the title of the question that opens.
Click Keep shifts.
Click Schedule in the top menu.
Use the arrow next to Today to go to tomorrow.
Read {Technician-A}'s shifts on {Work-order-1}, {Work-order-2} and {Work-order-3}.
results: Steps 4, 7 and 10: each drag opens the question "Clear {Technician-A}'s scheduled shifts?" (with the example name: "Clear Esther Howard's scheduled shifts?"). The line that is not approved ({Line-2}) and the declined line ({Line-4}) are ignored, and a Choose lines shift that ticks every approved line counts.
Steps 5, 8 and 11: after Keep shifts each work order moves to {Technician-B}'s column with the message "Lead technician updated".
Step 14: all three of {Technician-A}'s shifts are still on the Schedule tomorrow, at the same times.
new.source: Epic SV-10043; story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 49 (14 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S4-R28 (reworded in version 49 from Chris Ward's answer 1 of 14 Oct 2026 to our question sheet: only approved lines count, judged when the lead changes), S4-R29, S4-R23 and S4-R5, read 14 Oct 2026. Source-verified 14 October 2026. Not yet checked against a build.
quotes: The shift-clearing prompt (S4-R11, S4-R26) shows only when the outgoing lead has a work-order-level shift on this work order that has not ended. A work-order-level shift is one that covers every approved line of the work order, judged at the moment the lead changes; this is what the Schedule's Entire work order drop creates. Lines not yet approved, and declined lines, are ignored. On a work order with one line, a shift on that line counts, and so does a Choose lines shift that ticks every approved line. A shift on only some approved lines does not show the prompt, and that includes an Entire work order shift once a line has been added and approved after it was made.

The prompt reads: title “Clear {Name}'s scheduled shifts?” (with no name: “Clear the lead technician's scheduled shifts?”); text “{Name} has shifts scheduled for this whole work order. Clearing removes shifts that haven't started and ends one that's under way now. Shifts on individual lines and recorded time don't change.”; buttons “Keep shifts”, “Clear shifts” and “Cancel”.
If the user chooses to keep shifts, change the lead technician and retain the existing shifts.
S4-R5
After successful reassignment, show “Lead technician updated”; after unassigning, show “Lead technician removed”.

Customer {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST S4R28 Line Added") is used by this case only.

Work order {Work-order-1} (for example S10043-17651) for {Customer-A} is led by {Technician-A} and had two approved lines, {Line-1} (for example "Service - Full grease service") and {Line-2} (for example "Service - Adjust clutch"), when its shift was made.

quotes: The shift-clearing prompt (S4-R11, S4-R26) shows only when the outgoing lead has a work-order-level shift on this work order that has not ended. A work-order-level shift is one that covers every approved line of the work order, judged at the moment the lead changes; this is what the Schedule's Entire work order drop creates. Lines not yet approved, and declined lines, are ignored. On a work order with one line, a shift on that line counts, and so does a Choose lines shift that ticks every approved line. A shift on only some approved lines does not show the prompt, and that includes an Entire work order shift once a line has been added and approved after it was made.

The prompt reads: title “Clear {Name}'s scheduled shifts?” (with no name: “Clear the lead technician's scheduled shifts?”); text “{Name} has shifts scheduled for this whole work order. Clearing removes shifts that haven't started and ends one that's under way now. Shifts on individual lines and recorded time don't change.”; buttons “Keep shifts”, “Clear shifts” and “Cancel”.
S4-R5
After successful reassignment, show “Lead technician updated”; after unassigning, show “Lead technician removed”.
